title: TikTok: $42 billion left one bank in one day (SVB, Sam + detailed coded scenes)
_sources:
TikTok "$42 billion left one bank in one day" (Silicon Valley Bank, March 2023) -> project.json
Sources (checked 2026-10-26/27, same as YT 11):
Fed Vice Chair Barr, Senate testimony 28.03.2023 (via CNBC): $42B withdrawn on March 9, ~$100B scheduled for March 10 -> $142B of ~$175B deposits = 81%.
Wikipedia "Collapse of Silicon Valley Bank" (call report data): HQ Santa Clara, CA; ~86% of deposits uninsured; $1.8B loss on securities sale announced March 8 (evening);
  closed by California DFPI / FDIC receivership on the morning of March 10 (<2 days later); 3rd-largest US bank failure.
FDIC / Treasury / Fed joint statement 12.03.2023: systemic risk exception, all depositors fully protected.
FDIC: $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category.

lines.text: Forty-two billion dollars left this bank in one single day.
It was Silicon Valley Bank in California, the go-to bank for tech startups.
On March eighth, twenty twenty-three, it admitted a one-point-eight-billion-dollar loss on its bonds.
Founders panicked in group chats, and everyone pulled their money out with a few taps on their phones.
By the next morning, another hundred billion dollars was lined up to leave. That's eighty-one percent of all deposits.
So regulators shut the bank down, less than two days after the bad news.
And about eighty-six percent of the money was above the insured limit of two hundred fifty thousand dollars.
Then the government stepped in, and every single depositor got all of their money back.
